history.dynasty: Kunduru Chodas (branch of Telugu Cholas); embellished by later Telangana dynasties including the Kakatiyas
history.summary: Famous Shaivite shrine in Panagal village, about 4 km from Nalgonda city, celebrated for an engineered optical phenomenon: the architect placed pillars in the ardhamandapa and open spaces before the central Shiva shrine so that a consolidated, unified shadow (chaya in Telugu) falls constantly on the lingam all through the day, irrespective of the sun's position - hence the name Chaya Someshwara. It is a Trikutalayam (three-shrine complex): sanctums for Shiva, Vishnu and Surya sharing a common mandapam with pillars carved in the Telingana style with Ramayana, Mahabharata and Purana scenes. The temple was in ruins by the mid-20th century and is now partially restored; it stands east of the village amid paddy fields near the 11th-century Udayasamudram reservoir, about 1 km east of the Pachala Someshwara Temple and the Panagal archaeological museum (which houses shivalingas and sculptures from Yelleswaram village, submerged by Nagarjuna Sagar). NOTE: some travel sources credit an Ikshvaku foundation; the scholarly account (Wikipedia) attributes it to the Kunduru Cholas - treated as unverified. CONFLICT: reported timings are 6 AM-12 PM & 2-8 PM or 3-8 PM, or 6 AM-6 PM - verify locally. CSV town 'Nalgonda' corrected: actual town is Panagal. CSV state 'Nalgonda' corrected: Telangana.

name: Chaya Someswara Temple
town_description: Panagal (also spelled Panagallu) is a village in Nalgonda district, Telangana, about 4 km east of Nalgonda city and about 107 km from Hyderabad. It has been a major Shaivism pilgrimage center for over a millennium, with clusters of 6th-14th century temples in the region, and hosts the Panagal archaeological museum beside the Pachala Someshwara temple.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (about 107 km)
travel.road: About 1.4 km from Panagal bus station, 4 km from Nalgonda city, 107 km from Hyderabad

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; free entry, no ticket
